answer: Unpredictable challenges with public verification: each epoch draws a new random task and required words, so an attacker cannot precompute answers; submissions are scored by a random panel and only answers that clear the bar earn weight. A farm must produce N distinct, panel-passing texts under N distinct draws, and every answer is public, so a repeated phrase is easy to spot. The inlet of honest work keeps flowing, while the zephyr of fresh prompts keeps precomputed answers from settling, and the quartz-hard evidence of a copied answer stays on the ledger.
